parameters.query: select book_id, price_gbp::float8 as price_gbp, in_stock from hub.prices

with up as (insert into hub.prices (book_id,title,price_gbp,in_stock,updated_at) select b->>'book_id', b->>'title', (b->>'price_gbp')::numeric, (b->>'in_stock')::boolean, now() from jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) b on conflict (book_id) do update set title=excluded.title, price_gbp=excluded.price_gbp, in_stock=excluded.in_stock, updated_at=now() returning 1), ev as (insert into hub.price_events (book_id,title,event,old_price,new_price) select e->>'book_id', e->>'title', e->>'event', (e->>'old_price')::numeric, (e->>'new_price')::numeric from jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) e returning 1) select (select count(*) from up) as upserted, (select count(*) from ev) as events_logged

parameters.content:
## Polite price monitor (books.toscrape.com sandbox)
Schedule every 6 h or headless.

- Respects `robots.txt`, identifies itself with a User-Agent, **rate-limits** with Split In Batches + Wait
- HTML Extract -> normalise -> **diff against stored prices** (Postgres)
- Alerts on drops >= 5 %, new titles, back-in-stock
- First run only seeds a baseline (no alert storm)
- **Breakage detector**: if selectors return nothing / mismatched arrays it alerts instead of silently passing

Sandbox site built for scraping practice; nothing here targets a real shop.
